items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: If it’s not the most difficult tune in the world. If it’s “Waltz for Debbie” and you’ve never played it, then you need a chart

ctx.x: You hope, unless it’s sort of deceptive. © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

If it’s a really hard tune with a lot of keys I’ll say, “Can you write it out for me.” If I don’t get a chance to then I’ve just got to help make this happen. And sometimes if I’m really not getting it I’ll be looking at him like what is it? That’s just one of the hardest things about being in the rhythm section. Because often the piano players will get to say if it’s too hard. The piano players are very vocal about that, oh I really don’t know it. The piano players don’t want to be showing up not knowing chords…

And as far as a leader, it doesn’t serve the leader well either. Like I’m going to make you play it. Well okay but what you’re going to get you’re not going to be that happy with, it’s only going to reflect on you.
